read.thesis: AWS grew 36.7% to $42.2B with a $496B backlog and cash capex raised to ~$220B from ~$200B, while management says capacity still falls short of 2026 demand.

capex.quote: We now believe we will spend approximately $220 billion in cash CapEx in 2026. The higher cost of memory pushing this number up from our prior estimate of about $200 billion.

triggers.label: Cash capex $200B → $220B
triggers.quote: We now believe we will spend approximately $220 billion in cash CapEx in 2026.

triggers.label: AWS backlog $496B, triple-digit growth
triggers.quote: Our backlog stands at $496 billion, growing triple digits year-over-year.

triggers.label: AWS revenue +36.7% YoY
triggers.quote: Revenue growth of 36.7% year-over-year, accelerating for the fifth straight quarter

triggers.label: AWS operating margin 39.4%
triggers.quote: AWS operating margin of 39.4% reflecting disciplined efficiency gains and server capacity optimization.

triggers.label: Q3 operating income $22.5–26.5B
triggers.quote: Q3 operating income is expected to be between $22.5 billion and $26.5 billion.

guidance.quote: We now believe we will spend approximately $220 billion in cash CapEx in 2026.
Q3 net sales are expected to be between $197 billion and $202 billion.
Q3 operating income is expected to be between $22.5 billion and $26.5 billion.
we expect to more than double our fleet of robotic arms, like Cardinal and Sparrow, in 2026.

prior_guidance_check.quote: Earlier this year, we said we plan to invest approximately $200 billion in cash CapEx in 2026

red_flags.label: Free cash flow headwinds from capex
red_flags.quote: we'll spend a lot of CapEx and encounter free cash flow headwinds until these data centers come online

red_flags.label: Non-operating gain inflates EPS
red_flags.quote: primarily reflecting a $53.4 billion non-operating pre-tax gain from the valuation of the company's investment in Anthropic.

red_flags.label: Capacity short of 2026 demand
red_flags.quote: we will still not have enough capacity to meet all the demand we have in 2026

red_flags.label: Shipping cost inflation
red_flags.quote: we face heightened transportation costs driven by fuel inflation from the conflict in the Middle East

evasions.quote: We'll continue to look at all the options and make the appropriate decision at the right time, but nothing to share today.
Well, on the first question, Brian, we have so much demand right now.
